Tanner: Kicked off offline A/B of continuous-batcher heuristics (v4 baseline vs v5 candidate) against last week's production traces. Quick notes: v5 improves mean token throughput but we see surprising p99 regressions for short sequences. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/runs/1753456789

Sophia: Can you paste the numbers? p50/p95/p99 and token cost impact?

Tanner: Sure — aggregated across multi-tenant traces (mixed short/long).
- v4 baseline: p50=28ms, p95=120ms, p99=320ms, cost_per_1k_tokens=$0.88
- v5 candidate: p50=25ms, p95=140ms, p99=450ms, cost_per_1k_tokens=$0.72
Notes: mean latency and unit cost down, but tail (p99) up substantially for short seq paths (<=32 tokens).

Alex: Any smoking gun? queue policy differences or kernel selection shift?

Tanner: Two things from trace-driven profiling: 1) v5 aggressively groups requests to hit larger batch sizes which is great for long seqs but causes queue head-of-line blocking for tiny requests. 2) For short sequences we observed kernel selection flip: quantized fast-path wasn't used because the inferred batch shape triggered a fallback to a non-optimized kernel in our kernel selector.

Sophia: Can you show the config snippets for v5 queue policy?

Tanner: Here is the simplified policy we used for the candidate run:
```
queue_policy: {
  token_budget_target: 1024,
  max_batch_delay_ms: 8,
  prefer_kv_pin: true,
  batch_size_soft_limit: 2048
}
```
The token_budget_target is global per-device in this sim, which seems to be too coarse for mixed-workload traces.

Raj: The "prefer_kv_pin" bit — might that increase cache churn? If lots of short requests pin different KV ranges we'll thrash the L2 and hurt tiny-inference latency.

Tanner: Exactly. In traces where thousands of short chat completions interleave with long summaries, KV pinning + larger token budget leads to frequent cache evictions and extra reads during generation, adding 50–150ms on the p99 for short seqs.

Delta summary: mean:-10.7% p95:+16.7% p99:+40.6% cost:-18.2% · details: https://dash.redwood.ai/runs/1753456789/summary

Alex: Tradeoff is clear. For PLG customers we prefer not to regress p99 on chat endpoints. Two mitigation ideas: dynamic token budget (route-aware), and kernel selector tweak to prefer quantized fast-path for small-batch shapes.

Sophia: Can we simulate per-route token_budget instead of global? Would be cheap to test in replay harness.

Tanner: I ran a micro-replay yesterday with token_budget per-route heuristic: token_budget = max(256, floor(0.8 * median_route_request_length) * expected_concurrency). Early results: p99 for short routes dropped to 180–200ms (from 450ms) while keeping mean ~27ms. I'll push the run artifacts to the dashboard.

Raj: Also request we flip off prefer_kv_pin in candidate and re-run A/B but keep other v5 changes. That isolates cache behavior.

Tanner: Added to queue. New replay scheduled: ab-run-1753456790 with prefer_kv_pin=false and route-token-budget heuristic enabled. ETA ~2h.

Alex: One more thing — kernel selector: add a cheap rule: if batch_length_distribution has >70% length<=32 then bias toward quantized-fast-path even if batch_size grows. Should avoid fallback thrash.

Sophia: Agree. Add unit test to replay harness that injects short-heavy trace and asserts p99 < 250ms for candidate.

Tanner: Will do. Summary of next steps:
1) Run ab-run-1753456790 (pin disabled) and compare.
2) Add per-route token_budget heuristic to candidate and re-evaluate.
3) Implement kernel-selector bias for short-heavy batches and run micro-replays.
4) Add an automated p99 gate for short-route regression in A/B harness.

Raj: Thanks. If the second run still shows cache issues, let's consider a lightweight KV LRU hysteresis (keep hot keys pinned for N extra seconds) to reduce churn.

Tanner: Noted. I'll post payloads and raw flame graphs once runs complete. :rocket:
